subject: MSA / Order Form: deposit schedule, invoice entity & tax evidence
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@nimbushealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order form questions: deposit timing, invoice entity & tax evidence

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team reviewed the draft order form and had a few operational questions before we send this to legal:

- Deposit / prepay: the order form references a one-quarter advance invoice to satisfy the minimum commit. Can you confirm whether that deposit is refundable if we prepay and then reduce seat usage?
- Invoice recipient: we need the invoice to be issued to Nimbus Health, Inc. (US entity). The draft appears to list Redwood Software, LLC as invoice recipient — can you confirm the billing entity and whether we can route invoices to our AP team?
- Net terms: can we move Net 30 to Net 45 for initial pilots?
- Taxes: what documentation will Redwood need for tax/residency? Our tax team usually provides W-9 + VAT certificate when requested.

Attaching the draft order form with our inline ask (page 2 and payment schedule). Please advise next steps and who from your side will own the redlines.

Best,
Alex
Director of Procurement
Nimbus Health
[Attachment: Nimbus_OrderForm_v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form questions: deposit timing, invoice entity & tax evidence

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Looping in our commercial and legal leads to align on a concise response and propose language for the order form. See answers below; I’ve also attached a redline tracker so you can see proposed edits.

Quick answers:
- Deposit / prepay: generally non-refundable once applied against committed usage, but we can structure a capped credits approach for pilot reductions (see suggested paragraph in tracker).
- Invoice recipient: we can bill Nimbus Health, Inc. but need the legal entity mapped in the MSA / tax appendix so invoices flow to the correct entity for accounting.
- Net terms: can offer Net 45 for the pilot term only (90-day trial) but need to document on the order form and include fallback to Net 30 upon expansion.
- Taxes: we require standard tax residency evidence (W-9 for US entities; W-8BEN-E for foreign entities) and VAT reverse-charge confirmation where applicable.

Internal next steps: @kimberly — please propose final legal language around refundable vs. non-refundable deposits and the Net45 pilot carveout. @ben — can you propose a staged invoicing schedule (milestones) and a commercial concession if they prepay? @lauren — can you prepare the invoicing entity mapping checklist for finance?

Alex — attaching our redline tracker: OrderForm_redlines.xlsx. I’ll consolidate legal comments into a single redline for your review by Thursday.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OrderForm_redlines.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form questions: deposit timing, invoice entity & tax evidence

Mina / team — drafting proposed order form language below (legal suggested edits). Paste these into the redline tracker and I’ll finalize with Legal Ops.

1) Deposit / Prepayment paragraph (new):
"Deposit: Customer shall pay an advance payment equal to 25% of the annual committed spend (the \"Deposit\"). The Deposit shall be credited to Customer’s invoices over the first three billing cycles. Except as set forth in the next sentence, the Deposit is non-refundable. For a Pilot Period not to exceed ninety (90) days, in the event Customer reduces committed capacity by more than twenty percent (20%) during or immediately following the Pilot Period, Customer may elect to receive a credit for up to fifty percent (50%) of the Deposit, applied to future invoices. Any refund requests must be submitted within thirty (30) days of the end of the Pilot Period and are subject to Redwood’s approval and audit of usage."
2) Net terms carveout:
"Net Terms: Notwithstanding any contrary term in the MSA, the Parties agree that for the Pilot Period only, invoices will be payable Net 45. Upon expiration of the Pilot Period or following an upsell to production commitments, invoices will revert to the standard Net 30 payment term unless otherwise agreed in writing."
3) Invoice recipient / entity mapping (new appendix reference):
"Invoice Recipient: Customer shall identify the legal entity to receive invoices. Redwood will issue invoices to the specified entity and tax residency documentation must be provided prior to the first invoice. Change requests to the invoice recipient require a thirty (30) day notice and may require a revised order form."
4) Tax evidence requirement (operational):
"Tax Evidence: Customer shall provide applicable tax forms (W-9; W-8BEN-E; VAT registration certificate; or equivalent) within ten (10) business days of execution. Failure to provide required tax documentation may result in withholding or suspension of services. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide VAT invoices where applicable."
Comments: legal prefers credits over refunds for easier accounting; the Pilot credit compromise above is a middle ground. Also recommending we request procurement to use a PO number on the first invoice to expedite mapping in our ERP.

-Kimberly
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form questions: deposit timing, invoice entity & tax evidence

Team / Alex — consolidating here so we can move to a single redline. Proposed commercial package for Nimbus: 

- Payment schedule: 25% deposit (credited over first 3 invoices), then quarterly invoicing for committed baseline. For pilot customers: first two quarters invoiced Net 45, thereafter Net 30.
- Refunds vs credits: operationally we will issue account credits (not cash refunds). We’ll allow up to 50% credit on the Deposit if they downscale >20% within the 90-day pilot window (per Kimberly’s language).
- Invoicing entity: we can issue invoices to Nimbus Health, Inc. — please confirm full legal name and remit-to address and include PO on the first invoice.
- Taxes: require W-9 prior to first invoice; if they are EU/foreign, require W-8/W-8BEN-E and VAT registration for reverse-charge. If they cannot provide in time, we’ll withhold applicable taxes.
- Commercial concession: if Nimbus signs the final order form and returns the signed DocuSign by 31 Jan 2027, Redwood will apply a 5% one-time prepay discount to the first invoice (applied after credits).

Next steps: Mina — can you send the consolidated redline (OrderForm_redline_v2.docx) to Alex + procurement and propose a 30-min call to finalize (I recommend Thu 21 Jan 10am PT). Alex — can you confirm legal entity details and whether procurement can accept the credits workaround?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OrderForm_redline_v2.docx (DOCX)]
